code:
.text

.globl main

main:
    li $t0, 5
    li $t1, 10
    add $t2, $t0, $t1

    # exit
    li $v0, 10
    syscall
description: Load immediate integers into registers $t0 and $t1, add them into $t2, and exit with syscall 10.

steps.description: Under `.text` and `main:`, `li $t0, 5` loads 5 into `$t0`, `li $t1, 10` loads 10 into `$t1`, and `add $t2, $t0, $t1` stores their sum in `$t2`.
Lines 11-12 load service code `10` into `$v0` and invoke `syscall` to terminate the program.
Notice the operand order in `add $t2, $t0, $t1`: the destination register `$t2` comes first, followed by the two source registers `$t0` and `$t1`.

steps.answer: `$t2` holds 15 (`5 + 10`), and nothing is printed because the program only runs syscall 10 (exit).
steps.question: What value is stored in `$t2` after line 8 (`add $t2, $t0, $t1`) executes, and does the program print anything to the console?

steps.description: Line 8 adds `$t0` (5) and `$t1` (10) and writes `15` into `$t2`.
With `$v0` set to 10, `syscall` exits the program.

title: A First MIPS Program: Adding Two Registers
